100110101.text: Huh? It's not a holiday or anything, is it? Why's it so lively in here?

100110102.text: ...Prepare a few more strings of colored flags. As for the celebratory wine... I'll do the quality check in person.

100110103.text: This is our first award ceremony since the expeditionary force's triumphant return. We're looking to put on a show, you hear?

100110104.text: Leave it to us, Captain Kaeya!

100110106.text: Oh? The Honorary Knight and Paimon? Well, this saves me the trouble of sending someone to invite you.

100110107.text: I'm sure our colleagues from the expedition will be delighted to see such prestigious guests in attendance.

100110108.text: The Knights are giving out awards?

100110109.text: Well, I'm sure you know how many Knights bear unique titles, yes?

100110110.text: Take the Grand Master's "Boreas" or Captain Eula's "Spindrift," for example... Some they inherit. Others have unique origins...

100110111.text: But in the vast majority of cases, they are titles conferred to honor said knight's conduct and achievements.

100110113.text: Hmm... You could say that! Shame we were so busy with the issue of Dvalin's corruption back then, or we'd have held a ceremony for you, too... Let me think. Why don't we make it up to you this time?

100110114.text: It's fine, it's been so long, anyway.

100110115.text: Besides, isn't this ceremony meant for the knights who're back from the expedition in triumph? We wouldn't want to steal their thunder!

100110116.text: Plus, being honored guests is way more impressive than actually receiving a title! Y'know, makes us sound like big shots!

100110117.text: You might actually have a point there...

100110118.text: Is that so? In that case, I'm looking forward to seeing you at the ceremony.

100110119.text: By the way, who's getting titles this time around?

100110120.text: Mostly those who've made outstanding contributions during the expedition: Winfried, Leifhelm...

100110121.text: And Lohen, Vice Captain of the 5th Company.

100110122.text: Wait. Him? You mean he doesn't have one yet?

100110123.text: If it were just a question of personal ability, he'd have received a title before the expedition even started.

100110124.text: But he hasn't been with us for very long, and... Well, let's just say there are personal reasons for the delay.

100110125.text: Word is that he'll not only gain a title, but also official command over 5th Company.

100110126.text: Why, by my count, he's even set to break a certain someone's record.

100110129.text: "The youngest Captain of the Knights of Favonius," of course... The previous record holder was our former Cavalry Captain, Diluc.

100110130.text: Hehe. I wonder what face our "former Captain" will make when that happens.

100110131.text: I'm guessing he won't make any face.

100110132.text: Ah, ah, I wouldn't be so sure. He smiled oh-so-brilliantly the day he set that record...

100110133.text: A smiling champion of justice, huh...? Yeah, nah, Paimon can't see it...

100110134.text: Well, let's not dwell on that. Care to guess what title our dear Vice-Captain Lohen will receive?

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the Knights of Favonius Headquarters

100110201.text: ...Any questions about the award ceremony arrangements? Perhaps... Are you even listening?

100110204.text: Huh... Yeah. Can I go now? Thanks a lot, Grand Master!

100110206.text: *sigh*... What is it with you young people these days? When I first earned my title, I was so excited I couldn't sleep a wink all night...

100110207.text: Huh? Oh? And how many barrels of wine did you guzzle while counting sheep?

100110209.text: *sigh*... Forget it. I know you're not interested in a knightly title — or the position of Captain.

100110210.text: But it's Adorno's final wish to have you inherit the title of Benevolent Knight before he officially retires.

100110212.text: You've been back in Mondstadt for a while now, and you're usually stationed at Dornman Port... Have you not thought about going to see him?

100110213.text: ...Hey, there have been too many reports to file since our return from the expedition. I haven't been able to find the time.

100110214.text: Oh? Odd that the handwriting on the reports you've submitted looks rather like Gunther's, wouldn't you say?

100110215.text: Ugh... Can't even handle a little "paperwork"... He still needs more training.

100110216.text: Anyway — go have a good talk with Adorno. We'd like a smooth transition for both the title and the position of Captain.

100110217.text: Consider this a direct order from yours truly, the Grand Master, so don't go using work as an excuse, you hear?

100110219.text: Eh, don't look so worried. I've a rough idea of the agreement you two made before the expedition. If you need someone to cover for you...

100110220.text: ...I mean, considering Adorno's special circumstances, I can make an exception and go with you.

100110221.text: ...Uh, forget it. You two've worked together for so long, he'd see right through you with a glance.

100110222.text: *sigh* True... And besides, I've got other matters to attend to... Is there anyone else you can take?

100110223.text: Someone convincing, but not too close to Adorno... Do we have such a knight here in Mondstadt?

100110224.text: Hah, that "knight" you speak of... has just arrived.

100110227.text: I was troubled, troubled, I tell you, but then I just happened to see you two walking by from the window. This must be the Anemo Archon's guidance, don't you think?

100110228.text: Not at all! Paimon's not sure what's going on yet, but you just want us to help you scam someone, don't you?

100110229.text: Oh no, no, no, no, no, not at all! Honesty is a knight's badge of virtue. I'd just like you to "play the part" of my "friends."

100110230.text: ...And corroborate some of the expedition's events while you're at it. Relax. If I say a single lie... feel free to punch me, alright?

100110231.text: Wait. There's a ton of problems with that! We didn't even meet up with Varka until the very end of the expedition, and we didn't run into you in Nod-Krai, either...

100110232.text: Ah, right. Speaking of "friends," I've heard tell of a certain "friendly custom"...

100110301.text: Hey, old man! Still kicking, I see?

100110302.text: Heh. Didn't buy the farm during the expedition? Thought you might've fallen into some pit somewhere, what with how long it's taken you to come see me.

100110303.text: Ah, you worry too much. When it comes to pits, I've been the one doing all the digging and burying.

100110304.text: ...That's a novel way to say hello...

100110306.text: #My friend — the "Honorary Knight" — and {M#his}{F#her} guide, Paimon.

100110307.text: "Honorary Knight"... The same one that resolved the Stormterror incident...

100110310.text: #Oh, {M#he}{F#she} didn't just resolve that incident — {M#he}{F#she} helped us complete the expedition. The Wild Hunt, The Doctor, Andrius... {M#He}{F#She} played a part in dealing with all of them.

100110311.text: Oh? I've quizzed the knights at Dornman Port about what happened during the expedition.

100110312.text: Unfortunately, for some reason, none of them were willing to tell me the whole story... It's almost as if someone told them to avoid me.

100110314.text: Since we've got a moment, let's have a proper chat. How did this magnificent knight here end up making friends with you?

100110315.text: Hmm, I suppose it's because we both possess a "chivalric spirit" that shines as bright as Mora. Isn't that right, Paimon?

100110317.text: I've been keeping my promise to you, you know. For instance...

100110318.text: I've been organizing group training sessions with my fellow knights every week to build ironclad trust between "friends"...

100110319.text: Oh, right, the team building I told you about! Great way to foster trust and chemistry.

100110320.text: Hmm... As for this week's "training plan"...

100110321.text: (Drugging the wine one night in advance...)

100110324.text: What sorcery is this!? Huh? What do you mean, "there are no bullets in your gun"...

100110326.text: Surely the Vice-Captain can't take us all out if we swarm him at once? C'mon, let's get him— Aaah!

100110327.text: *scoff* Real combat's ten times harder than training, and the enemy's a hundred times more cunning than I am.

100110328.text: Remember this well. Once you're on the battlefield, the only one you can truly "trust" is yourself!

100110329.text: And so, to ensure the absolute safety of my "friends," I went out every night, eliminating potential threats around our stronghold...

100110330.text: Hmm... Vigilance and reconnaissance are indeed things a Company Captain needs to pay attention to...

subQuests.subQuestName: Serve as a witness for Lohen's expedition experiences

100110401.text: Yes, yes. Quality control for our drinks... That'll require a personal touch.

subQuests.subQuestName: Serve as a witness for Lohen's expedition experiences
Serve as a witness for Lohen's expedition experiences
Serve as a witness for Lohen's expedition experiences

100110601.text: Hah... Just ensuring my "friends" get a good night's rest. All in a day's work, you know?

100110602.text: Of course, in order to gather intel for the expeditionary force, I also needed to maintain my "connections" at all times... and communicate earnestly with my friends...

100110603.text: Haha, I didn't expect you to have matured so much from one trip...

100110604.text: Come, let me sprinkle some more salt on the cut...

subQuests.subQuestName: Follow Adorno to finish his work

100110701.text: Ah! The Benevolent Knight is here!

100110704.text: Hey now — no rushing, and no snatching! Easy now. Line up properly!

100110705.text: Eh, it's alright, it's alright. They're just kids. A little excitement is a good thing. Here you go. Today's candy.

100110708.text: ...Is this the "important work" you spoke of?

100110709.text: Oh, we're just getting started, "recruit." Try to keep up!

100110714.text: I should be the one asking you — how are you so skilled at this?

subQuests.subQuestName: Head to your destination and patrol

100110801.text: Weird, no signs of anything unusual here... Are there really monsters nearby?

100110802.text: If you're looking for the ones that have been behaving strangely, I fear you're here too late.

100110803.text: It seems someone beat the Knights of Favonius to the punch and took care of them already.

100110804.text: Diluc? What are you doing here?

100110805.text: #Long time no see, Mr. Adorno. You too, {NICKNAME}, Paimon... Lohen.

100110806.text: Uhm... Were the monsters here wiped out by a certain Darknight Hero by any chance?

100110809.text: ...I'm not personally familiar with this "Darknight Hero" you speak of, but based on the rumors I've heard, the traces left on this battlefield don't match his style.

100110810.text: This looks more like someone... obtained advance intel on the monsters and came to "clean up." Not even a single scrap remains.

100110811.text: Oh? So it would appear you're here to investigate, Master Diluc? That's odd. Why would the boss of the Dawn Winery be interested in monsters?

100110812.text: Dawn Winery's caravans pass through Dornman Port. The rumors left me ill at ease, so I decided to see for myself.

100110813.text: As for the Knights of Favonius... are they still understaffed even with the expedition's return?

100110814.text: Hah, strict as ever, I see. I took this patrol up myself — gotta keep moving while I still can.

100110815.text: I've been living this life for decades. Can't just sit idle, you know?

100110816.text: ...Thank you for your hard work, venerable Benevolent Knight.

100110817.text: ...Wait, what? Not even Varka gets that much respect from Diluc!

100110818.text: Heh. I'd say that's Varka's problem.

100110819.text: *sigh* Eroch only got away with causing that uproar by taking advantage of the Grand Master's absence.

100110820.text: If he and the Alder Knight had been here, they never would have allowed Crepus's heroism in driving off the dragon to go unrecognized.

100110821.text: ...And we old codgers back in Mondstadt wouldn't have been the only ones left to stand up for your father.

100110823.text: #Let's cut the small talk. Since there are no clues here, I have no reason to stay. Goodbye, {NICKNAME}, Paimon.

100110825.text: *sigh* Ursa... Eroch... Even when gone, some foes leave wounds that won't easily heal.

100110829.text: Hmm? Need me to explain? Sure. Ursa was a wicked dragon who could really take a beating, and Eroch was an Inspector who could've really used one...

100110830.text: *cough* ...Allow me instead. Ursa the Drake was a dragon who first appeared in Mondstadt a thousand years ago, bringing calamity with its immense might.

100110831.text: After the Knights of Favonius were founded, our first Grand Master, Vennessa, sealed it away with the Anemo Archon's help. After that, the dragon sank into slumber...

100110832.text: However, just a decade ago, it appeared in Mondstadt once again!

100110833.text: With the Grand Master away, its timing could not have been worse. Not only that, it would lie low when the Knights of Favonius mobilized to attack, only to suddenly reemerge when they were resting...

100110835.text: In the end, it was also "perfect timing" that the Fatui Harbinger who exterminated it just so happened to be "passing through."

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to assist in the experiment

100110901.text: Hmm... It's as we thought — the magic Miss Alice left behind isn't so easily understood.

100110905.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME}! Are you here to assist with the development tests for the Simulation Training Bubble: Type 02?

100110906.text: Is that... the magic bubble that can recreate memories?

100110908.text: I was told not long after my return that I could use this to catch up with the various events, large and small, that transpired during our absence.

100110909.text: ...But using this level of magic for... well, storytelling seems like a huge waste of resources.

100110910.text: You're not alone in thinking that. Our Investigation Team quickly recognized its broader potential for training simulations.

100110911.text: If we could recreate formidable enemies from senior knights' memories and incorporate them into realistic, safe training simulations, that could help raise the whole organization's combat prowess.

100110912.text: However, we've been debugging the bubble for a while now, and we still haven't fully grasped its underlying principles... We're also struggling to balance realism with safety...

100110913.text: "Safety"... doesn't sound like something Alice would give much thought to.

100110914.text: That so? Sounds interesting. Let me give it a shot.

100110915.text: You're not here to take part, are you, pops?

100110916.text: Oh, not to worry. I know exactly how much strength these old bones have left in them. I'm just here to provide the "memories" inside my head.

100110917.text: Oh? Then who was the tester in your original plan?

100110918.text: Miss Sucrose, the test arrangements are... Ah... Lohen?

100110921.text: I just happened to come along with Adorno to test this Simulation Training Bubble. I take it you're the scheduled tester?

100110922.text: Ah... Yes, that's right. And these are...

100110923.text: #*cough* Let me introduce you. These two are the Honorary Knight and {M#his}{F#her} guide, Paimon.

100110924.text: The Honorary Knight? I didn't expect someone so distinguished...

100110925.text: And this is Theodore, a trainee medic with the 8th Company. Like you, he's one of Lohen's friends.

100110927.text: No need to sound so surprised. I have plenty of "friends," don't I, Paimon?

100110929.text: (Paimon wonders how much this guy's "friendship fee" was...)

100110931.text: Theodore, isn't rescue and medical care more your thing? How did you end up getting roped into testing?

100110932.text: Uhm, I actually helped to construct this simulation, so I understand a few of its basic principles.

100110933.text: Besides, I trained to become a knight, too. And even if something happens, I should be able to patch myself up...

100110934.text: But you needn't force yourself to do this if Vice-Captain Lohen's willing to take over. We might get more practical test data from frontline knights too, so...

100110935.text: Y—Yeah, I suppose Lohen's the better pick...

100110936.text: Chin up, Theodore. If anything happens to Lohen, we'll be counting on you to treat him.

100110938.text: I doubt there's a memory out there that can hurt me... but let's get started, old man.

100111201.text: No fluctuation in pain parameters... Hmm. Should we switch to a more... normal test subject?

100111202.text: No need. Let's continue the test.

100111203.text: Are you sure? I don't think my memories will yield anything worth fighting against at this point...

100111204.text: Uh, don't we have a knight right here who's faced more terrifying foes?

100111205.text: Come on... Show me the Rächer of Solnari — as you remember him.

100111207.text: I'm not so disheartened that I'd fear his memory. I just wanna see...

100111208.text: If I'm still as... powerless as he claimed.

100111603.text: I'm fine... Just threw my back out... Gotta take a break, that's all... But Lohen...

100111605.text: Wound up hurting yourself from trying to hold back that final blow, didn't you...

100111606.text: Theodore, go get him checked over. Last thing we want is to miss a serious injury.

100111611.text: It's no big deal... Just got old. Things stick with you once you're over the hill, waiting to be set off by the slightest exertion... *sigh* Guess I'll have to ask Theodore for another prescription.

100111612.text: Is there... something up with Lohen?

100111613.text: Could there be a problem with the magic? But if there were issues with the reproduced memories, the Honorary Knight should have noticed...

100111616.text: Are you saying the problem... lies with Lohen himself?

100111617.text: ...Did the battle with the Rächer of Solnari set him off again...
